title: Planarian heads degenerated by barium regenerate adapted to it via a handful of genes

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Planarian heads degenerated by barium regenerate adapted to it via a handful of genes

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Planarian flatworms exposed to barium, a nonspecific potassium channel blocker, lose their heads but soon regenerate new heads completely adapted to barium, and transcriptomic analysis shows only a handful of genes up- or down-regulated, which Levin interprets as cells solving a problem in high-dimensional transcriptional space without an evolved response to barium.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: The Multiscale Wisdom of the Body: Collective Intelligence as a Tractable Interface for Next-Generation Biomedicine

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2025, The Multiscale Wisdom of the Body: Collective Intelligence as a Tractable Interface for Next-Generation Biomedicine › Intelligence Below the Cellular Level › The Inner Life of Active Matter

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Remarkably, they soon regenerate new heads which are completely adapted to the presence of barium [66]. Transcriptomic analysis reveals just a handful of genes that have been up‐ and down‐regulated to enable this feat of morphological and physiological homeostasis.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “The Multiscale Wisdom of the Body: Collective Intelligence as a Tractable Interface for Next-Generation Biomedicine”, BioEssays : news and reviews in molecular, cellular and developmental biology (2025), doi:10.1002/bies.202400196; section “Intelligence Below the Cellular Level › The Inner Life of Active Matter”. Scope: Planarian flatworms exposed to barium chloride (author's lab's prior work, ref [66])

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2025-wisdom-05: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.74

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The experimental regeneration and transcriptomic components are directly measurable and may have public sequence data. Existing data can check the result more readily than the stronger interpretation that cells solved a novel high-dimensional problem.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare head integrity and regeneration under continued barium exposure, then reanalyse transcriptomes for reproducible differentially expressed genes relative to exposed non-adapted and untreated worms. Recovery plus a small validated expression set supports the reported result; failure to recover or broad expression change refutes it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Completely adapted needs physiological as well as anatomical endpoints.

The problem-solving interpretation is not uniquely implied by differential expression.

The relevant accession is not identified in the batch.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.6
data adequacy: 0.65
analysis feasibility: 0.8
discriminating power: 0.75
operationalizability: 0.95

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The transcriptomic clause is directly reanalyzable: GSE98084 contains the adapted-head and control libraries, so the number of differentially expressed genes can be counted without new experiments. The anatomical claims, complete adaptation and absence of an evolved barium program, are not variables in that matrix and remain tied to one group's regeneration observations. The expression half can be resolved now; the full statement cannot.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Reanalyze the deposited head transcriptomes of barium-adapted versus control Dugesia and count genes that pass a pre-specified false-discovery threshold, then set that count beside the published head-loss and regeneration observations. A large coherent expression program would refute the handful-of-genes clause; a very small set would support it. The RNA-seq does not itself show that the new heads are morphologically normal or that no evolved barium response exists.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Head degeneration and morphological normality are not in the expression deposit.

One species and one lab's regeneration series limit the scope.

A small gene list is still compatible with an evolved ion-homeostasis response rather than an improvised solution.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.65
data existence: 0.75
operationalizability: 0.82
analysis feasibility: 0.8
data adequacy: 0.55

fields.label: Hypothesis
fields.value: In the public RNA-seq of planarians whose heads regenerated adapted to barium chloride (GEO GSE98084), only a handful of genes are differentially expressed between barium-adapted heads and control heads, i.e. a small fraction of the expressed transcriptome.

fields.label: Method
fields.value: fetch.py downloads the three GSE98084 supplementary workbooks and the series SOFT record; xlsx.py reads them with the standard library. analysis.py joins the two per-replicate FPKM files on transcript id (15,475 transcripts), keeps 15,446 with mean FPKM >= 1 in either group, and runs a Welch t-test on log2(FPKM+1), control (n = 2) vs BaCl2-adapted (n = 2), with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR, counting FDR < 0.05 and |log2FC| >= 1. As context it also counts transcripts with q < 0.05 and |log2FC| >= 1 in the authors' pooled and per-replicate Cuffdiff tables, and transcripts that change two-fold in the same direction in both replicate pairs.

fields.label: Pass criterion
fields.value: Pre-registered: with the deposited per-sample expression values, comparing barium-adapted head samples with untreated control head samples (Welch t-test on log2(CPM+1) per gene, genes with mean CPM >= 1 in either group, Benjamini-Hochberg FDR), the number of genes with FDR < 0.05 and |log2 fold change| >= 1 is <= 20, and is <= 0.2% of the tested genes.

fields.label: Fail criterion
fields.value: Pre-registered: >= 100 genes meet FDR < 0.05 and |log2 fold change| >= 1 in that comparison. Counts of 21-99 are pre-registered as 'mixed'. If either group has fewer than two replicate samples, or no per-sample quantification can be obtained or computed from the deposit, the verdict is 'inconclusive' (underpowered or data-unavailable).

fields.label: Unit
fields.value: transcripts with BH FDR < 0.05 and |log2FC| >= 1, BaCl2-adapted vs control heads (Welch t on log2(FPKM+1), 2 vs 2)

fields.label: Uncertainty
fields.value: 2 replicates per group; Welch t-test has ~1-2 degrees of freedom and very low power

fields.label: Interpretation
fields.value: Only the transcriptomic clause is tested: 'just a handful of genes up- and down-regulated' is mapped to the count of genes passing FDR < 0.05 and a two-fold change between barium-adapted and control heads, with 'handful' fixed in advance at <= 20 (the threshold proposed in the dataset-resolvability assessment). Head degeneration, complete adaptation and the claim that cells solved an unselected problem are not variables in the expression data and are not tested. The same finding is stated in levin-2023-agential-15 (Darwin's agential materials, 2023); this single test covers both claim ids and is filed under levin-2025-wisdom-05. If the deposit has additional groups (e.g. acute barium exposure before adaptation), their comparison with controls is reported as context only and does not enter the verdict. A t-test on few replicates has limited power, so the number of genes with |log2FC| >= 1 at nominal p < 0.01 is also reported as a sensitivity measure, not part of the verdict.

fields.label: Datasets
fields.value: GEO GSE98084: Regenerative adaptation to electrochemical perturbation in planaria (Dugesia japonica heads, 2 control, 2 BaCl2-adapted; Emmons-Bell, Durant, Martyniuk, Morokuma, Levin)

fields.label: Caveats
fields.value:
Deviation from the pre-registered rule, stated openly: the rule as written returns 'supports' (0 transcripts pass, <= 20), but the comparison could not have returned anything else. With two replicates per group the smallest FDR attainable across 15,446 transcripts was 0.11, so no transcript could reach FDR < 0.05 whatever the biology. A verdict that the data could not have contradicted is not evidence for the claim, so it is reported as inconclusive (underpowered). The pre-registration anticipated underpowering only for fewer than two replicates; it should have required a minimum attainable FDR.

The deposited data point away from 'a handful': the authors' own pooled Cuffdiff table lists 314 transcripts at q < 0.05 and >= 2-fold change (109 up, 205 down), above the pre-registered refute threshold of 100, and 1,981 transcripts change >= 2-fold in the same direction in both control/BaCl2 replicate pairs. Cuffdiff's pooled q-values model within-condition variance from only two libraries and were not the pre-registered statistic, so they do not enter the verdict, but they show that 'a handful' depends on the threshold. Counting Cuffdiff calls per replicate pair gives 4 and 18, which is near 'a handful'.

The series summary itself describes 'a number of ion translocators' and pathway-level enrichments of ~2-3-fold, which is closer to a moderate programme than to a handful of genes.

Not independent: GSE98084 is the Levin lab's own deposit for the study the claim cites (ref [66]). The reanalysis is independent of the authors' pipeline but not of their samples.

Units are Cufflinks transcripts (TCONS ids) on a D. japonica assembly, not collapsed genes; the deposited files appear pre-filtered to expressed transcripts (15,446 of 15,475 have mean FPKM >= 1). FPKM rather than counts was used, as pre-registered for deposits with only normalized values.

Only the expression clause is tested. Head degeneration, complete adaptation and the 'no evolved barium response' interpretation are not addressed. This test also covers levin-2023-agential-15, which states the same finding.
